doc.brief: A single-line text entry widget for use as a search entry.
doc.md:
A single-line text entry widget for use as a search entry.

The main API for interacting with a `GtkSearchEntry` as entry
is the `GtkEditable` interface.

It will show an inactive symbolic “find” icon when the search
entry is empty, and a symbolic “clear” icon when there is text.
Clicking on the “clear” icon will empty the search entry.

To make filtering appear more reactive, it is a good idea to
not react to every change in the entry text immediately, but
only after a short delay. To support this, `GtkSearchEntry`
emits the [`SearchEntry::search-changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#event:search-changed) signal which
can be used instead of the [`Editable::changed`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Editable#event:changed) signal.

The [`SearchEntry::previous-match`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#event:previous-match),
[`SearchEntry::next-match`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#event:next-match) and
[`SearchEntry::stop-search`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#event:stop-search) signals can be used to
implement moving between search results and ending the search.

Often, `GtkSearchEntry` will be fed events by means of being
placed inside a [`SearchBar`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchBar). If that is not the case,
you can use [`SearchEntry.set_key_capture_widget()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#method:set_key_capture_widget) to
let it capture key input from another widget.

`GtkSearchEntry` provides only minimal API and should be used with
the [`Editable`](xref:gtk:Gtk.Editable) API.

## Shortcuts and Gestures

The following signals have default keybindings:

- [`SearchEntry::activate`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#event:activate)
- [`SearchEntry::next-match`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#event:next-match)
- [`SearchEntry::previous-match`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#event:previous-match)
- [`SearchEntry::stop-search`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#event:stop-search)

## CSS Nodes

```
entry.search
╰── text
```

`GtkSearchEntry` has a single CSS node with name entry that carries
a `.search` style class, and the text node is a child of that.

## Accessibility

`GtkSearchEntry` uses the [`AccessibleRole.search_box`](xref:gtk:Gtk.AccessibleRole#value:search_box) role.

set_key_capture_widget.brief: Sets `widget` as the widget that `entry` will capture key events from.
set_key_capture_widget.md:
Sets `widget` as the widget that `entry` will capture key
events from.

Key events are consumed by the search entry to start or
continue a search.

If the entry is part of a `GtkSearchBar`, it is preferable
to call [`SearchBar.set_key_capture_widget()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchBar#method:set_key_capture_widget) instead,
which will reveal the entry in addition to triggering the
search entry.

Note that despite the name of this function, the events
are only 'captured' in the bubble phase, which means that
editable child widgets of `widget` will receive text input
before it gets captured. If that is not desired, you can
capture and forward the events yourself with
[`EventControllerKey.forward()`](xref:gtk:Gtk.EventControllerKey#method:forward).

activate.brief: Emitted when the entry is activated.
activate.md:
Emitted when the entry is activated.

The keybindings for this signal are all forms of the <kbd>Enter</kbd> key.

next-match.brief: Emitted when the user initiates a move to the next match for the current search string.
next-match.md:
Emitted when the user initiates a move to the next match
for the current search string.

This is a [keybinding signal](class.SignalAction.html).

Applications should connect to it, to implement moving
between matches.

The default bindings for this signal is <kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>g</kbd>.

previous-match.brief: Emitted when the user initiates a move to the previous match for the current search string.
previous-match.md:
Emitted when the user initiates a move to the previous match
for the current search string.

This is a [keybinding signal](class.SignalAction.html).

Applications should connect to it, to implement moving
between matches.

The default bindings for this signal is
<kbd>Ctrl</kbd>+<kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>g</kbd>.

search-changed.md:
Emitted with a delay. The length of the delay can be
changed with the [`SearchEntry:search-delay`](xref:gtk:Gtk.SearchEntry#property:search-delay)
property.

search-started.brief: Emitted when the user initiated a search on the entry.
search-started.md: Emitted when the user initiated a search on the entry.

stop-search.brief: Emitted when the user stops a search via keyboard input.
stop-search.md:
Emitted when the user stops a search via keyboard input.

This is a [keybinding signal](class.SignalAction.html).

Applications should connect to it, to implement hiding
the search entry in this case.

The default bindings for this signal is <kbd>Escape</kbd>.
